payload.title: AI Builders Daily · 2026-08-30
payload.summary:
**Sight restoration is leaving the lab**: Max Hodak says Science’s Prima retinal implant now has Europe approval and first sales are weeks away; Brain-computer interfaces shift from moonshot talk to actual patients reading books and solving puzzles; On the AI builder side, the mood is split: product teams hint at launches, while founders warn of model-price wars, compute shortages, and a sea of lookalike apps.
**看点不绕弯**：Max Hodak 那条线最硬，失明患者重获部分视觉，Prima 已拿下欧洲批准，离真正卖货只差临门一脚；AI 圈今天更像情绪大乱斗，一边在憋大招，一边开始担心算力涨价、额度收紧；另一股更真实的抱怨也冒出来了：新产品越来越多，但长得都像，权限越要越狠，真正新的东西反而不够多。

sections.headline: **fx** 0.0.7 improves **MCP** support and CLI execution / **fx** 0.0.7 强化 **MCP** 支持与 CLI 执行
sections.body:
https://t.co/OL0LzGtvAw **fx** 0.0.7: 

- hugely improved **MCP** support, eval'd with top **MCPs** like @context7ai, @datadoghq, @mongodb, @linear, @notionhq, @supabase, @neondatabase, @stagehanddev, @usekernel…

- more minimalist: fewer tools and improved shell execution. One of the trickiest things about **CLI agents** is that running commands is actually not that simple.

e.g: commands might hang or run for very long, their output needs to be monitorable by the agent, they might produce huge amounts of output, or none. 

This is an area where **fx** really shines and will continue to get better.

https://t.co/OL0LzGtvAw **fx** 0.0.7：

- **MCP** 支持大幅增强，已经用一批顶级 **MCP** 做过评估，比如 @context7ai、@datadoghq、@mongodb、@linear、@notionhq、@supabase、@neondatabase、@stagehanddev、@usekernel……

- 设计更克制了：工具更少，shell 执行也更好了。**CLI agents** 最棘手的地方之一，就是“执行命令”这件事其实一点都不简单。

比如：命令可能会卡住，或者跑很久；它们的输出得能被 agent 持续监控；输出可能巨大，也可能什么都没有。

这正是 **fx** 特别出色的地方，而且还会继续变强。

sections.headline: AI products all look the same now · 现在的 AI 产品越看越像
sections.body:
Never had so many AI products looked so similar

Even though the number of products is exploding, there aren't that many radical new ideas and everything blurs into each other

Every time I open this app it feels like homework: yet another new product to learn that promises to do the same thing but somehow better; the specific ways in which it's better isn't clear unless you invest hours actually trying it

从来没觉得这么多 **AI** 产品会长得这么像。

虽然产品数量在爆发式增长，但真正激进的新点子并没有那么多，结果就是一切都开始糊成一团，彼此越来越分不清。

每次我打开这个 app，都像在做作业：又来一个新产品，要你重新学一遍。它也说自己做的是同一件事，只是“更好”一点；但到底好在哪儿，往往根本说不清，除非你真的花上几个小时亲自去试。

sections.headline: Resist dunking, keep building 抵制嘲讽，继续做事
sections.body:
Resist dunking*

I see it WAY too much with folks especially today. It’s the perfect dopamine loop - other people join in and you feel great. But, it just screams envy and doesn’t lead to anything productive. 

Sure, you can pat yourself on the back and say “see I told you so” but how did it move the world? Nowhere. If you think you can do it better, go do that then. Screaming about someone’s unfair advantages is not going to change your life - and probably leads to more sadness. 

Keep building. Continue to change the world. That’s the best way to have impact. Choose kindness above all else. 

* the only caveat here is if you’re calling out obvious fraud, or pointing out something that’s woefully bad, do it. there are very clearly some businesses that are going to be vaporware and if you have evidence call it out. that doesn’t scream envy, it’s factual and not dunking by any means.

别老想着嘲讽别人*

这种事我看到太多了，尤其是现在。它就是一种完美的多巴胺循环：别人一起跟着起哄，你就会感觉特别爽。但这只会暴露出嫉妒，产不出任何真正有用的东西。

当然，你可以拍拍自己说一句“看吧，我早就说过”，可这对世界有什么推动吗？没有。如果你觉得自己能做得更好，那就去做。对着别人的不公平优势大喊大叫，不会改变你的人生，反而大概率只会让你更难受。

继续做事。继续去改变世界。这才是产生影响力最好的方式。无论如何，先选择善意。

* 这里唯一的例外是：如果你是在揭穿明显的欺诈，或者指出某些离谱到不行的问题，那就该说。有些公司明摆着就是空气项目，如果你有证据，就直接点出来。这不是嫉妒，这是基于事实，也根本不算嘲讽。

items.source_label: Podcast episode: From Restoring Sight to Reimagining the Brain, with Max Hodak

sections.headline: **Prima** restores functional vision, now moving into Europe commercial rollout / **Prima** 恢复功能性视力，开始在欧洲商业化落地
sections.body:
Max Hodak says **Science** is fundamentally a medical device company focused on using a better understanding of the brain to produce unusually large medical outcomes. Its lead product, **Prima**, is a retinal prosthesis he compares to a cochlear implant for the eye: a tiny chip sits under the retina, while glasses project images onto the implant to bypass damaged photoreceptors and send visual signals back into the brain.

Max Hodak 说，**Science** 本质上是一家医疗器械公司，核心是用对大脑更深的理解，做出传统医学里少见的大效果。公司的主力产品 **Prima** 是一种视网膜假体，他把它比作“眼睛的人工耳蜗”：把微型芯片植入视网膜下方，再通过眼镜把图像投到芯片上，绕过失效的感光细胞，把视觉信号重新送回大脑。

He highlights a recent milestone: **Prima** received European marketing approval in July 2026, making commercial sales possible in Europe within weeks. The discussion frames this as a rare case where a brain-computer-interface-adjacent technology is no longer just a distant moonshot, but an actual product entering the market.

他特别提到一个关键节点：**Prima** 已在 2026 年 7 月拿到欧洲上市批准，意味着几周内就能正式开始销售。节目里把这件事看作一个很少见的拐点: 脑机接口相关技术不再只是远期概念，而是已经走到真实产品和真实市场。

sections.headline: Why the retina first: faster path, clearer engineering loop / 为什么先做视网膜：路径更快，工程闭环更清晰
sections.body:
Hodak explains that **Science** started with several ideas after **Neuralink**, including biohybrid neural interfaces that use living neurons rather than metal wires or genetic modification. But that work needed a nearer-term business. The team concluded that restoring vision was the highest-value goal they could realistically pursue with the resources and field maturity available in early 2021.

Hodak 解释说，离开 **Neuralink** 后，**Science** 一开始并行看过几条路线，包括用活体神经元而不是金属电极或基因改造来做生物混合神经接口。但这类研究周期太长，必须配一个更近线的业务。团队最后判断，在 2021 年初的技术成熟度和资源条件下，恢复视力是最有价值、也最有机会落地的方向。

From there, they evaluated multiple entry points for vision restoration, including the retina, the **LGN** in the thalamus, and visual cortex, along with gene therapy, electrical stimulation, and ultrasound. He says the retina was the right place if the optic nerve still exists. **Science** later acquired the French company **Pixium**, whose technology originated at **Stanford**, because it had the most advanced retinal electrical stimulation program they saw.

之后他们系统评估了多种视觉恢复入口，包括视网膜、丘脑里的 **LGN**，以及视觉皮层，也比较了基因治疗、电刺激和超声等方案。他的判断是，只要视神经还在，最佳切入点就是视网膜。后来 **Science** 收购了法国公司 **Pixium**，其技术最早来自 **Stanford**，因为在他们看来，那是当时最领先的视网膜电刺激方案。

sections.headline: The brain as a computer, and a roadmap beyond vision / 把大脑当作计算机，以及超越视觉的路线图
sections.body:
A central theme of the episode is Hodak’s blunt claim that the brain is a computer. His argument is that medicine often struggles when it tries to solve problems through deep molecular understanding alone, while interfaces with the nervous system can produce immediate, visible effects. He contrasts the uncertainty of long drug-discovery cycles with examples like cochlear implants, deep brain stimulators, and motor-cortex implants that can enable usefully observable behavior quickly.

这期节目的核心观点之一，是 Hodak 很直接地把大脑定义为一台计算机。他的意思是，医学如果只靠深入分子机制去解题，常常又慢又不确定；但只要能和神经系统建立接口，很多效果是立刻可见的。他拿人工耳蜗、脑深部刺激、运动皮层植入做对比，强调这类系统往往能在很短时间内产生明确、可观察的结果。

He positions **Prima** as an existence proof rather than an endpoint. Today it has a narrow field of view and black-and-white output, but he says the engineering path to better grayscale and even some color, at least red and green, is visible. He also places the product inside a broader 10-to-15-year pipeline spanning vision, biohybrid neural interfaces, and a perfusion program called **Vessel**, all aimed at a larger medical revolution and, ultimately, more flexible ways for the brain to interface with the world.

他把 **Prima** 定义为“可行性证据”，不是终点。现在它的视野还比较窄，成像也只有黑白，但他认为提升灰度层次、甚至做出部分颜色感知，至少红和绿，已经能看到工程路径。再往大了看，他把这项产品放进一个 10 到 15 年的总路线图里：视觉、生物混合神经接口，以及一个叫 **Vessel** 的灌注项目，目标都是推动更大范围的医学跃迁，并最终让大脑和外部世界建立更灵活的连接。
